primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: SLC4A4 encodes NBCe1-A, the electrogenic sodium-bicarbonate cotransporter on the basolateral membrane of proximal tubular cells. Loss impairs basolateral Na+/HCO3- exit and therefore transepithelial bicarbonate reabsorption, causing autosomal recessive proximal renal tubular acidosis often accompanied by ocular abnormalities.
vignette: A child has growth failure and persistent hyperchloremic non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis. Urine becomes appropriately acidic after plasma bicarbonate falls, indicating intact distal acidification. The child also has glaucoma and band keratopathy. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC4A4.
lead: Which renal transport process is most directly impaired?
correct: Basolateral electrogenic sodium-bicarbonate cotransport in proximal tubular cells
distractors: Apical sodium-hydrogen exchange in proximal tubular cells
Apical hydrogen-ion secretion by alpha-intercalated cells
Basolateral chloride-bicarbonate exchange in alpha-intercalated cells
Apical chloride-bicarbonate exchange in beta-intercalated cells
distractor_notes: NHE3 contributes to proximal sodium and bicarbonate reclamation, but SLC4A4 encodes the basolateral NBCe1 transporter rather than the apical sodium-hydrogen exchanger.
Alpha-intercalated-cell apical proton secretion is a distal-nephron process and remains intact in isolated SLC4A4 proximal RTA.
AE1-mediated basolateral chloride-bicarbonate exchange in alpha-intercalated cells is associated with distal RTA, not SLC4A4 proximal RTA.
Pendrin-mediated apical chloride-bicarbonate exchange in beta-intercalated cells is unrelated to the SLC4A4 proximal-tubule defect.
key_expl: NBCe1-A, encoded by SLC4A4, mediates basolateral electrogenic sodium-bicarbonate transport in proximal tubule cells and is essential for transepithelial bicarbonate reabsorption. Loss causes proximal RTA and can produce ocular disease.
objective: Link SLC4A4-related proximal RTA to defective basolateral NBCe1-mediated sodium-bicarbonate cotransport in proximal tubular cells.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Complete plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 deficiency due to SERPINE1 loss
mechanism: PAI-1, encoded by SERPINE1, inhibits tissue-type and urokinase-type plasminogen activators. Complete deficiency causes excessive conversion of plasminogen to plasmin and excessive fibrinolysis, producing delayed bleeding after trauma or surgery despite normal routine coagulation tests.
vignette: A teenager has recurrent delayed bleeding several hours after dental extractions and minor surgery but little spontaneous bleeding. Prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, and thrombin time are normal. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SERPINE1.
lead: Which hemostatic abnormality most directly explains the bleeding tendency?
correct: Failure to inhibit tissue- and urokinase-type plasminogen activators, causing excessive plasmin generation
distractors: Failure to activate factor X through the tissue-factor pathway
Loss of platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa-mediated aggregation
Failure to cross-link fibrin because of factor XIII deficiency
Loss of von Willebrand factor-mediated platelet adhesion
distractor_notes: Tissue-factor pathway defects prolong coagulation testing and are not the mechanism of SERPINE1 deficiency.
GPIIb/IIIa defects cause Glanzmann thrombasthenia with a primary platelet-aggregation defect rather than delayed hyperfibrinolytic bleeding.
Factor XIII deficiency can also cause delayed bleeding but reflects defective fibrin cross-linking, not loss of PAI-1-mediated control of plasminogen activation.
von Willebrand disease causes defective platelet adhesion and often mucocutaneous bleeding, not the specific fibrinolytic defect established by SERPINE1 loss.
key_expl: PAI-1 normally restrains fibrinolysis by inhibiting tPA and uPA. Complete SERPINE1 deficiency permits excessive plasmin generation and clot breakdown, classically causing delayed post-traumatic or postsurgical bleeding with normal PT and aPTT.
objective: Link complete PAI-1 deficiency to excessive fibrinolysis caused by failure to inhibit plasminogen activators.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Giant axonal neuropathy due to GAN loss of function
mechanism: GAN encodes gigaxonin, a BTB-Kelch protein that controls turnover of specific proteins by targeting them for proteasomal degradation. Loss of gigaxonin causes accumulation of cytoskeletal intermediate filaments, including neurofilaments, producing giant axons and progressive neurodegeneration.
vignette: A child develops progressive sensorimotor neuropathy, ataxia, and tightly curled hair. Nerve biopsy shows markedly enlarged axons packed with disorganized neurofilaments. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in GAN.
lead: Which cellular function is most directly impaired?
correct: Targeting intermediate-filament proteins for proteasomal degradation
distractors: Anterograde transport of synaptic vesicles by kinesin
Retrograde transport of neurotrophic signals by dynein
Assembly of myelin basic protein in oligodendrocytes
Synthesis of neurofilament proteins on free cytosolic ribosomes
distractor_notes: Kinesin-mediated axonal transport is distinct from gigaxonin-dependent protein turnover.
Dynein-mediated retrograde transport is not the primary molecular function of gigaxonin.
Myelin basic protein assembly does not explain neurofilament-packed giant axons from GAN loss.
The defect is impaired turnover rather than increased synthesis of neurofilaments.
key_expl: Gigaxonin targets selected proteins, including intermediate-filament components, for proteasomal degradation. GAN loss causes abnormal intermediate-filament accumulation in neurons and glia.
objective: Link GAN-related neurodegeneration to failure of gigaxonin-mediated turnover of intermediate-filament proteins.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
discipline: Bone Biology / Endocrine Signaling / Medical Genetics
mechanism: Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia is caused by gain-of-function PTH1R variants that constitutively activate the PTH/PTHrP receptor in a ligand-independent manner, producing skeletal dysplasia and PTH-like mineral-ion effects despite suppressed endogenous PTH.
vignette: A child has short-limb short stature, bowed legs, metaphyseal widening, hypercalcemia, and recurrent nephrolithiasis. Serum parathyroid hormone is suppressed. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous pathogenic variant in PTH1R.
lead: Which molecular effect most directly causes this disorder?
correct: Constitutive ligand-independent activation of the PTH/PTHrP receptor
distractors: Loss of PTH1R function causing failure of PTH and PTHrP signaling
Constitutive activation of the calcium-sensing receptor
Loss of fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 signaling
Failure of vitamin D receptor binding to calcitriol
distractor_notes: PTH1R loss-of-function variants cause different skeletal phenotypes such as Blomstrand dysplasia or primary failure of tooth eruption, not Jansen disease.
CaSR activation tends to lower serum calcium and does not explain the PTH-like skeletal/mineral phenotype.
FGFR3 loss causes skeletal overgrowth phenotypes rather than Jansen metaphyseal dysplasia.
Vitamin D receptor defects cause hereditary vitamin D-resistant rickets with low effective calcitriol signaling, not constitutive PTH1R signaling.
key_expl: Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia is a PTH1R gain-of-function disorder. Pathogenic variants lock the receptor in an active state, producing ligand-independent signaling even when endogenous PTH is suppressed.
objective: Associate Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with constitutive ligand-independent PTH1R activation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: ALPK3 is an atypical cardiac pseudokinase that functions as a scaffold at the sarcomeric M-band and nuclear envelope. Loss disrupts localization of myomesins and other M-band proteins and impairs sarcomeric proteostasis, producing hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy.
vignette: A young adult with unexplained hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and myocardial fibrosis is found to carry a pathogenic protein-truncating variant in ALPK3. Functional studies show loss of ALPK3 protein.
lead: Which normal role of ALPK3 is most directly disrupted?
correct: Scaffolding M-band proteins such as myomesins to maintain sarcomeric proteostasis
distractors: Phosphorylating troponin I as an active serine-threonine kinase
Forming calcium-release channels in the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Anchoring intermediate filaments to cardiac desmosomes
Catalyzing ATP-dependent actin-myosin cross-bridge cycling
distractor_notes: Current functional studies indicate ALPK3 behaves as a pseudokinase; its major identified role is scaffolding rather than catalytic phosphorylation.
Ryanodine receptors form sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium-release channels, not ALPK3.
Desmoplakin anchors intermediate filaments to desmosomes; ALPK3 is an M-band/nuclear-envelope scaffold.
Myosin ATPase drives cross-bridge cycling and is unrelated to ALPK3 scaffolding.
key_expl: ALPK3 localizes to the sarcomeric M-band and functions as a scaffold supporting myomesin localization and sarcomeric protein homeostasis. Loss disrupts M-band organization and causes cardiomyopathy.
objective: Link ALPK3 cardiomyopathy to loss of M-band scaffolding and sarcomeric proteostasis rather than kinase catalysis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: MYO5B encodes myosin Vb, an actin-based motor/tether that cooperates with Rab8/Rab11 recycling pathways to deliver and recycle apical cargo in polarized enterocytes. Loss disrupts apical membrane trafficking and brush-border protein localization, causing severe congenital diarrhea and characteristic microvillus inclusions.
vignette: A neonate develops intractable watery diarrhea and severe failure to thrive within days of birth. Small-intestinal biopsy shows loss of the apical brush border and intracellular microvillus inclusions in mature enterocytes. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in MYO5B.
lead: Which cellular process is most directly impaired?
correct: Rab-dependent trafficking and recycling of cargo to the apical membrane of enterocytes
distractors: SNARE-mediated release of neurotransmitter vesicles at presynaptic terminals
Clathrin-mediated endocytosis of LDL through the LDL receptor
Dynein-dependent retrograde transport along neuronal microtubules
COPII-mediated export of newly synthesized proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum
distractor_notes: Presynaptic neurotransmitter exocytosis is a neuronal vesicle-fusion process and is not the MYO5B enterocyte trafficking defect.
LDL-receptor endocytosis is a distinct clathrin-dependent pathway and does not explain the apical polarity/brush-border phenotype.
Dynein-mediated neuronal retrograde transport is unrelated to myosin Vb-dependent apical recycling in enterocytes.
COPII exports proteins from the ER to the Golgi; MYO5B disease primarily disrupts post-Golgi/recycling-endosome delivery of apical cargo.
key_expl: Myosin Vb cooperates with Rab8/Rab11-associated recycling pathways to maintain polarized apical trafficking in enterocytes. MYO5B loss mislocalizes brush-border proteins and produces the hallmark microvillus-inclusion phenotype.
objective: Link MYO5B-related microvillus inclusion disease to defective Rab-dependent apical membrane trafficking and recycling in enterocytes.

outline: Familial hyperaldosteronism type I / glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Unequal crossing over between CYP11B1 and CYP11B2 creates a chimeric gene in which the ACTH-responsive CYP11B1 promoter drives CYP11B2 aldosterone-synthase coding sequences. Aldosterone synthase is ectopically expressed in the zona fasciculata and aldosterone production becomes ACTH dependent.
vignette: A 17-year-old has early-onset hypertension, hypokalemia, suppressed plasma renin activity, and elevated aldosterone. Several relatives have young-onset hypertension. Genetic testing identifies a chimeric CYP11B1/CYP11B2 gene.
lead: Which molecular consequence most directly explains this disorder?
correct: ACTH-responsive expression of aldosterone synthase in zona fasciculata cells
distractors: Angiotensin II-independent constitutive activation of the mineralocorticoid receptor
Loss of 11-beta-hydroxylase activity with accumulation of deoxycorticosterone
Constitutive activation of the calcium-sensing receptor in zona glomerulosa cells
Loss of epithelial sodium-channel activity in the distal nephron
distractor_notes: The disorder is caused by altered regulation of aldosterone synthase, not constitutive mineralocorticoid-receptor activation.
11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency causes congenital adrenal hyperplasia with excess deoxycorticosterone and reduced aldosterone/renin signaling rather than a CYP11B1-promoter/CYP11B2-coding fusion.
Calcium-sensing-receptor activation is not the mechanism of familial hyperaldosteronism type I.
ENaC loss causes aldosterone resistance with salt wasting and hyperkalemia, the opposite physiologic pattern.
key_expl: In familial hyperaldosteronism type I, a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene places aldosterone synthase under an ACTH-responsive promoter. Aldosterone is therefore produced ectopically in the zona fasciculata in an ACTH-dependent fashion.
objective: Link glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism to a CYP11B1-promoter/CYP11B2-coding fusion that makes aldosterone synthesis ACTH dependent.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: SLC25A15 encodes ORNT1, the mitochondrial ornithine transporter that moves cytosolic ornithine into the mitochondrial matrix. Loss deprives the urea cycle of intramitochondrial ornithine, causing hyperammonemia, hyperornithinemia, and homocitrullinuria.
vignette: A child develops episodic confusion and vomiting after high-protein meals. Plasma ammonia and ornithine are elevated, and urine contains homocitrulline. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC25A15.
lead: Which transport process is most directly impaired?
correct: Import of ornithine from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
distractors: Export of citrulline from the mitochondrial matrix to the cytosol
Import of pyruvate into the mitochondrial matrix
Export of aspartate from mitochondria through the malate-aspartate shuttle
Import of long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria through the carnitine shuttle
distractor_notes: Citrulline export participates in the urea cycle but is not the SLC25A15/ORNT1 defect.
Mitochondrial pyruvate transport is mediated by the MPC complex and is unrelated to HHH syndrome.
Aspartate transport uses different mitochondrial carriers and does not produce the HHH biochemical triad.
The carnitine shuttle transports fatty acyl groups, not ornithine.
key_expl: ORNT1, encoded by SLC25A15, transports ornithine into the mitochondrial matrix. Loss limits mitochondrial ornithine availability for the urea cycle and produces the classic HHH biochemical triad.
objective: Link HHH syndrome to defective mitochondrial ornithine import through SLC25A15/ORNT1.

mechanism: Neyman bias occurs when a case-control study samples prevalent rather than incident cases and exposure affects both disease occurrence and disease-related survival. Cases who die or recover before sampling are missed, so the exposure distribution among observed cases is distorted.
vignette: Investigators study whether a particular exposure is associated with a rapidly fatal disease. They identify cases by surveying all people currently living with the disease on a single date rather than enrolling newly diagnosed cases. The exposure increases both disease incidence and early disease-related mortality, so many exposed patients die before they can be sampled as cases.
lead: Which bias most directly threatens the estimated exposure-disease association?
distractors: Berkson bias
Recall bias
Lead-time bias
Observer-expectancy bias
distractor_notes: Berkson bias arises from admission-related selection of hospital cases/controls; the defining problem here is preferential survival among prevalent cases.
Recall bias requires differential reporting of prior exposures rather than selective survival to the case-sampling date.
Lead-time bias affects apparent survival after earlier detection and does not arise from prevalent-case sampling in a case-control study.
Observer-expectancy bias requires measurement or interpretation influenced by investigator expectations, which is not described.
key_expl: Sampling prevalent cases preferentially captures people who survive long enough to be observed. When exposure also affects disease-related mortality, the observed exposure distribution among cases is distorted; this is Neyman, or prevalence-incidence, bias.
objective: Recognize Neyman prevalence-incidence bias when prevalent-case sampling selectively excludes rapidly fatal exposed cases.

system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
outline: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
mechanism: VALUE is a structured family-conference communication strategy: Value family statements, Acknowledge emotions, Listen, Understand the patient as a person, and Elicit family questions.
vignette: During an ICU family conference, the physician explicitly affirms what family members say, acknowledges their distress, listens without interrupting, asks about the patient's values and identity outside the hospital, and ends by inviting all remaining family questions.
lead: Which communication framework is being used?
distractors: NURSE
SPIKES
Best Case/Worst Case
CUS
distractor_notes: NURSE is an empathy framework centered on naming, understanding, respecting, supporting, and exploring emotion; the full family-conference sequence here maps to VALUE.
SPIKES structures delivery of bad news and does not use the family-centered VALUE sequence.
Best Case/Worst Case uses scenario planning around treatment trajectories rather than the VALUE family-conference behaviors.
CUS is a team safety-escalation tool using concerned, uncomfortable, and safety-issue statements.
key_expl: The sequence directly maps to VALUE: Value family statements, Acknowledge emotions, Listen, Understand the patient as a person, and Elicit questions.
objective: Recognize VALUE as a structured communication strategy for ICU family conferences.
